issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, despite conventions requiring tests for every feature and unauthorized-call/tamper tests for each Livewire action.
save(), delete() and transfer() are declared `: void` but return a redirect response, which is a PHP fatal error and makes the Settings component unloadable.
`use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;` is imported twice, causing a 'name is already in use' compile error; the membership model cannot be loaded.
addMember() never calls $this->authorize, so an employee (who can mount the page via 'view') can add members; the task explicitly requires employees to get 403.
The target role is an enum but is compared with the string 'admin', so the condition is always true and transfer() always aborts 403 instead of transferring ownership.
The owner check compares the enum-cast role with a string and never matches, so an owner membership can be deleted (including by its owner or an admin), violating 'never removes the owner'.
assignRole() allows targeting the owner's membership and demoting it to admin/employee, leaving the entity without an owner; no guard protects the owner row.
Membership IDs from the client are resolved without verifying `entity_id === $this->entity->id`, so a manager can mutate memberships belonging to a different entity they also manage.
The last-manager guard counts managers globally, so removing an ordinary employee from an entity with one owner is also blocked with 403; it should only guard removals of a manager.
owner() is declared to return HasOneThrough but hasOne() returns HasOne, so accessing the relation raises a TypeError.

The contract requires the HasFactory and SoftDeletes traits, but the models only reference `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\HasFactory`/`SoftDeletes` attributes (the sibling User model uses the trait); soft deletes and `Entity::factory()` are therefore unreliable or missing.

entities() passes hasManyThrough keys 'entity_id'/'id', which joins entities.entity_id to memberships.id instead of entities.id to memberships.entity_id, so the relation is wrong (and queries a nonexistent column).
The definition omits entity_id and user_id and tries to set them in afterCreating, which runs after the INSERT; the NOT NULL foreign keys make `EntityMembership::factory()->create()` fail.
owner_seq is added as a default (virtual) generated column, but the task requires a stored generated column, so the schema does not meet the specified contract.
None of the Settings write actions re-authorizes server-side; the Livewire policy requires every public action to call `$this->authorize(...)`, not rely solely on mount().
Public input properties have no #[Validate] rules and $targetMembershipId is never validated, contrary to the project's Livewire validation pattern.

All new screen text is hardcoded English instead of coming from lang/*/ui.php, and the required 'Transferir propriedade'/'Transfer ownership' lang key is missing (only nav and owner-notice keys were added at lang/en/ui.php:46-48, lang/pt_BR/ui.php:46-48).
`{{ $m->role }}` tries to echo a UserRole enum and raises a TypeError, while `$m->role=='admin'` comparisons never disable the buttons; the members page will not render.

This large rewrite removes framework documentation and adds an unrelated providers/aliases block (including a nonexistent Eloquent facade and providers not added by this change), far outside the task.

The provider extends `Illuminate\Auth\AuthServiceProvider`, which has no `registerPolicies()` method or $policies handling (that belongs to the Foundation AuthServiceProvider), so booting it fails or policies are never registered.
For a duplicate member the code displays the `validation.exists` message ('selected email is invalid'), which misleadingly says the user does not exist.
New page routes use `Route::get(Component::class)` while the project's sibling routes use `Route::livewire(...)`; this is inconsistent and may not match the installed Livewire API.
Both models use `$guarded = []`, which disables mass-assignment protection instead of deliberately declaring fillable attributes as the conventions require.
The schema doc adds the membership table but never documents owner_seq as a column, and CHANGELOG.md is not updated as the docs-in-sync convention requires.
There is dead code ($userId is assigned but unused) and several unused imports, adding noise without behavior.
delete() soft-deletes the entity and deletes memberships outside a transaction, so a failure between the two writes can leave the data inconsistent.
The email input has no label or accessible name (placeholder only), and the new views use no Bulma classes or Blade components, unlike the project's UI conventions.
Property indentation is inconsistent and several new files lack a trailing newline.

review.summary: The change adds the entity models/migrations/policies, entity pick controller, Livewire dashboard/members/settings pages, routes and translations. It cannot be approved: Settings.php and EntityMembership.php contain PHP fatal errors, ownership transfer and owner protection are broken by enum/string comparisons, addMember is unauthorized, the model/factory/soft-delete contract is not met, there are no tests, and a large unrelated config/app.php rewrite is included.
